title: Screens
appliesWhen: The product has screens a person uses (web, app, or a tool with a visual interface). Left out for a product with no screens, such as a command-line tool or an API.

questions.ask: Which devices and screen sizes must the product work on, and which one matters most?
questions.why: Sets the widths every key screen is rendered at, and which one is designed first.

questions.ask: Which screens matter most to you: the ones a user sees first, uses most, or where money or trust is at stake?
questions.why: These are the key screens designed and approved before the build; the rest follow their pattern.

questions.ask: Are there existing screens, a design file or a component library the new screens must match or reuse?
questions.why: Existing screens are a reference to compare against, not something to redesign unasked.

questions.ask: Which languages will the screens be shown in, and does any read right to left?
questions.why: Text length and direction change layouts; a screen approved in one language can break in another.

questions.ask: Is real content available (product names, prices, photos, sample records), or must it be written or made?
questions.why: Screens are judged with real content; placeholder text hides the layout problems real text causes.

questions.ask: Is there an accessibility level the product must meet beyond the default (WCAG 2.2 level AA)?
questions.why: A stricter level changes contrast, sizes and motion on every screen.

questions.ask: Should screens have transitions or animation, and how much?
questions.why: Motion is design work and runtime cost; none, light and rich are three different builds.

criteria.mustBeTrue: The look was chosen from rendered variations of the same screen, and the choice is recorded.

check.how: The variations are rendered files and the design direction file names the one chosen and when.

criteria.mustBeTrue: Every key screen is rendered in the chosen look, at each width named in the Q&A.

check.how: The list of key screens is compared with the rendered files: one file per screen per width, none missing.

criteria.mustBeTrue: Every step of every journey in the experience document has a screen.

check.how: Each journey step in the experience document is matched to a screen in the screen list; a step with no screen is listed.

criteria.mustBeTrue: Each key screen is shown in every state it can be in: empty, loading, filled, and error.

check.how: The screen list names the states of each key screen and each state has a rendered file.

criteria.mustBeTrue: The screens use only the colours, typefaces and sizes of the brand's design tokens.

check.how: A search of the screens' styles finds no colour value, font name or size that is not a token.

criteria.mustBeTrue: Every key screen shows real product text and content in the users' languages, with no placeholder text.

check.how: Each rendered key screen is read; lorem ipsum, 'TODO' or untranslated text fails it.

criteria.mustBeTrue: Each key screen holds its layout in the language with the longest text, with nothing cut off or overlapping.

check.how: Each key screen is rendered in the longest language named in the Q&A and looked at for cut or overlapping text.

criteria.mustBeTrue: No key screen scrolls sideways at the narrowest width named in the Q&A.

check.how: A browser at that width reports a page no wider than the window for each key screen.

criteria.mustBeTrue: Text on every key screen has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5 to 1 against what is behind it (3 to 1 for large text).

check.how: An accessibility scan of each rendered key screen reports no contrast failure (WCAG 2.2, 1.4.3).

criteria.mustBeTrue: Everything a user taps or clicks is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, or has that much space around it.

check.how: An accessibility scan of each rendered key screen reports no target-size failure (WCAG 2.2, 2.5.8).

criteria.mustBeTrue: Where the Q&A named existing screens or a component library to match, the new screens reuse its components and differ only where the owner agreed.

check.how: Each new key screen is set beside the named reference; every difference is listed with the reason. Passes without a comparison when the Q&A named nothing to match.

outputs.title: Look variations
outputs.what: The same screen rendered in several looks, for the owner to choose from.

outputs.title: Screen list
outputs.what: Every screen of the product with the journey steps it serves, its states, and whether it is a key screen.

outputs.title: Key screens, rendered
outputs.what: Each key screen in the chosen look, at each width and in each state, as files the build is compared against.

logic: Every state shown (empty, loading, filled, error) is behaviour the product must produce and test.
Every action on a screen (a button, a form, a link) is an operation the system must provide.
What a screen shows is data the system must store and return: the screen list is the first draft of the data model.
assets: Images, icons and illustrations used on the screens, in the sizes each width needs.
runtime: The heaviest key screen sets the page-weight and load-time budget.
Lists that can grow (a feed, search results, a table) need paging or lazy loading; the screen shows which.
Transitions and animation, where the Q&A asked for them, set a frame-rate budget on the slowest named device.
